subject: Nanotechnology
title: Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
description: A quick win: understand Piezoelectric Nanogenerators.

hook.text: Walk on a floor and generate electricity — ZnO nanowire arrays convert footstep pressure into power.

buildup.text: Bending a piezoelectric nanowire separates positive and negative charges — creating voltage across its length.

discovery.text: Zhong Lin Wang invented the nanogenerator in 2006 — proving nanoscale mechanical energy can be harvested usefully.

twist.text: Each nanowire generates picowatts — millions are needed in parallel for microwatt-level useful output.

climax.text: Self-powered nano sensors run on vibration energy alone — no batteries, no wires, just ambient motion.

punchline.text: Bend a nanowire and it gives you electricity — motion becomes power.

quiz.question: How do piezoelectric nanogenerators harvest energy?
options: They absorb light and convert it to electricity
Mechanical deformation of piezoelectric nanowires separates charges, generating voltage
They use magnetic fields to induce current in nanowires
